newsitem.title: USA: NYS comptroller plans bill to raise pension payout.
newsitem.headline: NYS comptroller plans bill to raise pension payout.

text.p: The New York State Comptroller told New York public retirees he is planning to draft a bill that would link their benefits to how well the state pension fund performs, the Albany Times Union said on Thursday.

The plan would give retirees a three-percent raise when the fund yielded more than 10 percent a year, a benchmark H. Carl McCall said had been matched or exceeded by all New York public retirement systems in eight of the past nine years.
The paper said state lawmakers were intrigued by McCall's proposal for funding pension raises at no direct cost to state or local government or taxpayers.

But the Times Union added Sheldon Silver (D-Manhattan), the Assembly Speaker, noted to another local newspaper, the Daily Gazette, that the more public retirees take from the retirement system, the less state and local governments save in the form of lower pension contribution rates for future retirees.
Silver and the Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno (R-Troy), said they would take a serious look at the comptroller's plan, the Times Union added.
